channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Justiça Eleitoral pelo Brasil: TREs se mobilizam para as eleições de outubro
item.description: The Electoral Justice intensifies preparations for the October 2026 elections across Brazil. In Tocantins, electoral court staff are undergoing advanced training on electoral systems and disinformation, while in Mato Grosso, polling stations — mainly schools — are being inspected to ensure readiness for voters.

item.title: Crise na Nicarágua e declaração de Ortega inflamam debate político nas redes, aponta levantamento
item.description: Statements by Nicaraguan President Daniel Ortega, claiming there will be no more elections to prevent the opposition from taking power, sparked intense debate on Brazilian social media, with over 675,000 interactions in 24 hours across X, Instagram, and Facebook. The topic reached 7th place in Brazil’s X Trending Topics, and Ortega was searched over 50,000 times on Google Trends Brazil, with opposition figures linking him to President Lula to demand stronger stances, while government supporters emphasized Itamaraty’s diplomatic approach toward authoritarian regimes.

item.title: Ala do PSDB articula candidatura própria em SP
item.description: A São Paulo wing of the PSDB is articulating an independent candidacy for former senator José Aníbal in the 2026 gubernatorial race, defying the party’s national directive to support Tarcísio de Freitas’ (Republicanos) re-election. The effort is led by long-standing party figures seeking an alternative to the current governor.

item.title: Não vamos sair da mesa de negociação, diz Lula sobre tarifaço de Trump
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva stated that Brazil will not withdraw from negotiations with the United States regarding tariffs imposed by the Trump administration on Brazilian products. He emphasized the importance of dialogue to resolve trade disputes and protect national interests.

item.title: PP e União Brasil decidem manter neutralidade sobre apoio a Flávio
item.description: The União Progressista federation, formed by Brazil Union and Progressistas, has decided to maintain neutrality regarding support for Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) in his pre-candidacy for the Presidency of the Republic, allowing its state directories to define positions autonomously. While the São Paulo section has already declared support for Bolsonaro, PP senators met with the party's national president, Ciro Nogueira, in Brasília to discuss the matter, whose final stance remains to be formalized by the federation's leadership.

item.title: Centrão não sente em Flávio Bolsonaro o aroma do poder
item.description: Despite having an ascending candidacy in February, Flávio Bolsonaro failed to consolidate political support by the eve of the convention that would formalize his presidential bid. He has yet to name a running mate or form a coalition, revealing weakness in his political maneuvering within the Centrão and difficulty securing strategic alliances. The absence of key political arrangements suggests his presidential project lacks the 'scent of power' needed to advance strongly in the 2026 elections.

item.title: Renan Santos critica falas de Flávio sobre urnas: “Vergonha”
item.description: Renan Santos, presidential candidate from the Missão party, criticized Senator Flávio Bolsonaro’s (PL–RJ) claims about vulnerabilities in Brazil’s electronic voting machines, calling them an 'international embarrassment' and suggesting they may constitute political self-sabotage. Renan acknowledged that while Brazil’s electoral system could be improved, it remains functional, democratic, and a potential model for other nations.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro nega irregularidades de seu escritório com empresa ligada a Vorcaro
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro denied that his law office issued R$1.5 million in invoices to companies linked to banker Daniel Vorcaro, and stated he did not receive funds from Copenhagen Consultoria e Assessoria S.A.

item.title: Brasil pediu aos EUA que sobretaxa de 12,5% não seja cumulativa
item.description: The Lula government asked the U.S. to ensure that a proposed 12.5% tariff on Brazilian goods over alleged forced labor is not cumulative with existing duties, which could otherwise reach a total of 37.5%. Officials state the third edition of the Brazil Sovereign Plan, backed by R$18.5 billion, is sufficient to counter the impact and a fourth version is unnecessary. Negotiations with the U.S. continue, with a follow-up round expected after the USTR’s final tariff announcement this Friday (Jul 24).

item.title: Ala tucana se rebela contra apoio a Tarcísio e quer lançar Aníbal ao governo de SP
item.description: A historical faction of the São Paulo PSDB is articulating an independent candidacy for the state government, rejecting support for Governor Tarcísio de Freitas. The chosen name is former senator José Aníbal, positioning him as an alternative to the party’s current alignment. The move reflects internal divisions within the party over its political direction for 2026.

item.title: Moraes autoriza visita de Rogério Marinho a ex-comandante da Marinha na prisão
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes authorized a visit by Senate opposition leader Rogério Marinho to imprisoned former Navy Commander Almir Garnier Santos. The request was made by the defense and granted by the minister.

item.title: Em plenária, centrais sindicais reforçam mobilização pelo fim da 6 X 1
item.description: Trade union centrals held a national virtual plenary to strengthen mobilization for ending the 6x1 work schedule and approving the PEC that reduces the weekly workweek from 44 to 40 hours, already passed by the Chamber and awaiting Senate vote. The union movement advocates dialogue with Congress, avoiding confrontation, and sees party conventions as opportunities to influence senators. The measure is backed by Lula as an electoral trump card and also by Chamber President Hugo Motta.

item.title: PT prepara ação na Justiça contra Flávio Bolsonaro por declarações sobre urnas a embaixadores
item.description: The Workers' Party (PT) is preparing a legal action before the Electoral Justice against Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) for statements made to foreign ambassadors, in which he linked Brazil's electronic voting system to allegations of fraud in Venezuelan elections and claimed Brazilian machines originated from the Venezuelan company Smartmatic. The PT argues the claims are false and may constitute an electoral crime, as the TSE has repeatedly stated that Brazilian electronic voting machines are developed and operated solely by the Electoral Justice, with no ties to Smartmatic. The lawsuit is expected to be filed between Wednesday and Thursday.

item.title: Flávio faz vídeo de IA com versão criança e exibe faixa presidencial
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro posted an AI-generated video in which he dialogues with a child version of himself, asking whether he should continue trying in politics and receiving an affirmative response, ending with him wearing the presidential sash. The video mirrors a viral Neymar Jr. AI clip and continues the Bolsonaro family's trend of using AI for symbolic political storytelling.

item.title: Papo Antagonista: as múltiplas notas de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, senator and pre-candidate for presidency, had his law firm flagged for issuing invoices to companies linked to accountant Rogério Lourenço Novo, alleged operator of shell companies used by businessman Daniel Vorcaro to move funds from Banco Master. The allegations suggest possible use of corporate structures for illicit money laundering purposes.

item.title: TSE propõe 'Selo Maria Vai com as Urnas'
item.description: The TSE president proposes an 'electoral accuracy seal' in response to advocates of printed and auditable voting, linking the proposal to the January 8, 2023 movement. The author criticizes the initiative as a populist artifice that artificially breeds distrust in the popular vote, presenting it as a ruptural solution with the same genetic basis as election fraud allegations.

item.title: Irmão de Michelle ironiza: “Não se meta!”
item.description: Eduardo Torres, brother of Michelle Bolsonaro, defended his sister in an indirect response to former deputy Eduardo Bolsonaro, who criticized the release of a video in which Michelle disclosed tensions with Senator Flávio Bolsonaro. Torres replied sarcastically on social media with the phrase “Don’t interfere!”, without naming names directly. The post was published on O Antagonista.

item.title: Priscila Costa anuncia candidatura à Câmara
item.description: Deputy Priscila Costa (PL-CE), an ally of former first lady Michelle Bolsonaro, announced her candidacy for re-election to the Chamber of Deputies in 2026 following a meeting with PL national president Valdemar Costa Neto. She stated that her Senate bid was harmed by Michelle Bolsonaro's departure from the presidency of PL Mulher.

item.title: Com voto de Mendonça, STF nega recurso da Universal e anula doação de fiel
item.description: The STF formed a majority to deny Universal's appeal and annul a believer's donation, upholding the TJ-MG ruling that classified the donations as resulting from irresistible moral coercion. The decisive vote came from Minister André Mendonça during the judicial recess, joining Fachin, Cármen Lúcia, Alexandre de Moraes, Cristiano Zanin and Dias Toffoli. The IURD was ordered to repay BRL 229,100 in donations, plus BRL 12,000 in moral damages, with interest and adjustment.

item.title: Caiado critica fala de Flávio Bolsonaro a embaixadores contra as urnas: 'Dava para atrair investimento'
item.description: PSD presidential candidate Ronaldo Caiado criticized Senator Flávio Bolsonaro's (PL-RJ) remarks against electronic voting machines on social media, stating such comments deter investment and harm Brazil's image. He emphasized that trust in the electoral system is crucial for attracting foreign capital and maintaining institutional stability.

item.title: Lula cobra reciprocidade dos EUA e diz que Brasil não deixará mesa de negociação
item.description: President Lula criticized the lack of reciprocity in trade negotiations with the United States, stating Brazil made proposals and sought dialogue but faced American resistance despite facing 25% tariffs on Brazilian products. He announced R$15 billion from Brazil Soberano 2 and R$18.5 billion in credit for exporters, aiming to diversify markets and uphold national sovereignty amid the U.S. decision, which Brazil views as politically and ideologically motivated.

item.title: TSE pede que TREs firmem parcerias para fortalecer a análise técnica de casos de desinformação eleitoral
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) has directed regional electoral courts (TREs) to establish technical cooperation agreements with institutions specializing in artificial intelligence, digital forensics, and content analysis to strengthen the fight against electoral disinformation in the 2026 elections. The initiative aims to enhance the technical capacity of the Electoral Justice in producing evidence for cases involving disinformation and synthetic content, ensuring greater legal security in their analysis. The measure aligns with TSE Resolutions No. 23.610/2019 and 23.755/2026.

item.title: PP e União Brasil comunicam neutralidade a Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The Progressistas and União Brasil federation announced neutrality in the 2026 Brazilian presidential election, undermining Flávio Bolsonaro’s efforts to form an alliance with the two parties. The decision, communicated by PP leader Senator Ciro Nogueira, applies to the first round and may extend to the second, stemming from deteriorating relations after Federal Police operations and lack of mutual support. The move also dampens hopes for Republican Party backing, which is likely to mirror the neutrality due to PL’s lack of support for its candidates in state races.

item.title: Apelação de Bolsonaro contra inelegibilidade pelo TSE segue parada na mesa de Fux
item.description: Jair Bolsonaro's appeal against his ineligibility, imposed by the TSE in 2023 for political abuse of power and misuse of communication media, remains stalled in the rapporteurship of Minister Luiz Fux at the STF since March 2025. Even if the appeal were granted, Bolsonaro would remain ineligible due to another 2023 electoral conviction and, primarily, a 27-year-and-three-month prison sentence for leading a coup attempt, which, under the Clean Record Law, bars him from running for eight years after serving the sentence.

item.title: Gestão Tarcísio vai à Justiça para abrigar dependentes químicos em CDHU
item.description: The Tarcísio de Freitas administration went to court to secure the implementation of a monitored housing program for chemically dependent individuals who have completed treatment, to be housed in CDHU-managed residential complexes. The initiative aims to integrate health and housing policies to support social reintegration through structured follow-up.

item.title: Áudio: Acessibilidade será a maior da história nas eleições de 2026
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) announced that over 1.9 million people with disabilities will be able to vote in the 2026 elections, a record number making this the most accessible election in Brazilian democratic history. Senator Mara Gabrilli (PSD-SP), who is tetraplegic, emphasized the importance of guaranteeing voting rights for people with disabilities, reinforcing the commitment to electoral inclusion.

item.title: Eduardo diz que tarifaço dos EUA é fruto de “má-fé” de Lula
item.description: Eduardo Bolsonaro accused President Lula of bad faith in trade negotiations with the U.S., claiming that Lula’s refusal to engage properly led to the imposition of 25% tariffs on Brazilian goods. He argued that Lula avoids criticizing China or Europe to prioritize a political clash with Donald Trump, using a hypocritical discourse of sovereignty defense to gain electoral support.

item.title: Caiado sobre Eduardo e Flávio: Pateta da Disney é inofensivo; o do Brasil tropeça nos EUA
item.description: PSD presidential pre-candidate Ronaldo Caiado criticized former deputy Eduardo Bolsonaro by comparing him to a 'harmless Disney Goofy,' stating that the 'Brazilian political Goofy' trips in the United States. The remark was made on social media X on Monday, the 21st, following the Trump administration's decision to grant a green card to Eduardo Bolsonaro. Caiado used the metaphor to question the credibility and international impact of Brazilian right-wing figures.

item.title: Campanha do PT usa Pix, tarifaço e terras raras para bater em Flávio
item.description: The PT's campaign, launched today under the slogan 'Brazil does not surrender', targets Flávio Bolsonaro using three pillars: Pix, tariff hikes, and rare earths. The launch date coincides with the enforcement of 25% U.S. tariffs on Brazilian goods, leveraging the current economic climate to reinforce a narrative of national sovereignty defense.

item.title: Lula cita falta de reciprocidade em diálogo com EUA, mas diz que Brasil não abandonará mesa de negociações
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva criticized the lack of reciprocity in trade talks with the United States but affirmed Brazil will remain at the negotiating table. He announced R$18.5 billion in credit for companies affected by the 25% U.S. tariffs on Brazilian products and signed a law allocating an additional R$15 billion to the Brazil Sovereign Plan, expanding the government’s response to the U.S. trade measures.

item.title: Lula venceria eleição no 1º turno no RN, diz pesquisa
item.description: An AtlasIntel/94 FM poll conducted in Rio Grande do Norte between July 16–21, 2026 shows Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva would win the 2026 presidential election in the first round with 56.9% of votes, ahead of Flávio Bolsonaro at 28.5%. Lula’s government has 55% approval and 42% rate his administration as excellent or good.

item.title: Ciro Nogueira comunica Flávio Bolsonaro que PP e União Brasil ficarão neutros em eleição presidencial
item.description: PP president Ciro Nogueira informed Flávio Bolsonaro that the PP-União Brasil federation will remain neutral in the 2026 presidential election, possibly repeating the stance in the second round. The decision was driven by the need to allow parties to form state-level alliances, lack of enthusiasm for Bolsonaro’s candidacy, and concerns over allegations linking him to banker Daniel Vorcaro.

item.title: Governo Lula amplia o Plano Brasil Soberano com R$ 18,5 bilhões para empresas atingidas pelo tarifaço
item.description: President Lula’s government expanded the Brazil Sovereign Plan with R$18.5 billion in new financing lines for companies impacted by U.S. tariffs, comprising R$13.5 billion from the National Treasury and R$5 billion from BNDES, intended for working capital, investment, innovation, and market access. The measure covers sectors such as agriculture, mining, chemicals, textiles, and automotive, and was formalized by sanctioning the law that converted the original provisional measure, expanding its reach to cooperatives and associations. BNDES will design the allocation plan, to be reviewed by an interministerial council, targeting strategic sectors and exporters affected by U.S. Sections 232 and 301 trade measures.

item.title: Nunes Marques defendeu urnas a embaixadores antes de fala de Flávio
item.description: TSE President Kássio Nunes Marques defended the integrity of Brazil's electronic voting machines on June 16, emphasizing their development by electoral justice officials and manufacturing by Positivo Tecnologia, along with public audits. Flávio Bolsonaro, on July 21, repeated misinformation by claiming Smartmatic manufactures Brazilian voting machines, though his advisors denied he questioned the system's integrity, stating he only cited public facts. The TSE reiterated on July 22 that Brazilian machines are not made by Smartmatic but are domestically designed and produced.

item.title: Flávio e Jair Bolsonaro lideram rejeição no RN, diz AtlasIntel
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) is the most rejected political figure in Rio Grande do Norte, with 60.5% rejection, followed by former president Jair Bolsonaro (PL) at 55.7%, according to an AtlasIntel/94 FM poll released on July 22, 2026. President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) ranks seventh with 33.3% rejection. The survey interviewed 1,245 voters between July 16 and 21, with a 3-point margin of error and 95% confidence level.

item.title: Escritório de Flávio emitiu e cancelou notas para empresas usadas em esquema de Vorcaro
item.description: The law office of Senator Flávio Bolsonaro issued and canceled two invoices worth R$500,000 each, totaling R$1 million, in favor of a shell company used by Daniel Vorcaro to move R$58 million from Banco Master, according to an investigation by Metrópoles.

item.title: Kassio orienta tribunais a buscar especialistas em IA para agilizar identificação de conteúdo adulterado
item.description: The president of the TSE, Kassio Nunes Marques, directed state electoral courts to establish partnerships with AI-specialized institutions to speed up the detection of altered content during the 2026 election campaign. The initiative aims to combat disinformation and safeguard the integrity of the electoral process.

item.title: Lula sobre tarifaço: "Nunca encontramos reciprocidade na negociação"
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva stated that Brazil found no reciprocity in negotiations with the United States over the 25% tariffs imposed on Brazilian exports. He emphasized that Brazil will remain at the negotiating table but will not yield to U.S. pressure, instead choosing to pursue new markets rather than complain about unsold goods.

item.title: 'Nosso time': Justiça determina exclusão de post que reúne Lula, ACM Neto e ex-ministro de Bolsonaro na Bahia
item.description: Brazil's Electoral Justice ordered Meta to remove an Instagram and Facebook post falsely associating President Lula with Bahia gubernatorial candidate ACM Neto and Senate candidate João Roma, using an unmarked digital montage with the phrase 'this is our team'. Judge Mhercio Cerqueira Monteiro ruled the post constituted fabricated content intended to mislead voters and harm political opponents, violating electoral law and TSE resolutions. The decision also mandates removal of monetization and disclosure of the poster's personal data for possible referral to the Electoral Public Prosecutor's Office.

item.title: Flávio repete Bolsonaro ao atacar urnas, mas há uma diferença
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro echoed his father Jair Bolsonaro’s claims by alleging that Brazil’s electronic voting machines share the same origin as those used in Venezuela and are part of a purported fraud scheme cited in a CIA report, during a meeting with foreign ambassadors.

item.title: Lula diz que Brasil não encontrou reciprocidade em negociação sobre tarifaço: 'Ninguém vai ganhar do Brasil mentindo'
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva stated that Brazil has not found reciprocity in negotiations with the United States over the 25% tariff on Brazilian goods, which took effect this Wednesday. Although he described the U.S. decision as 'abrupt', Lula emphasized that Brazil will remain at the negotiating table, having already submitted proposals and personally engaged in discussions in Washington. He added that 'no one will gain from Brazil by lying', underscoring a firm but diplomatic stance without abandoning dialogue.

item.title: Pivô de crise no PL, Priscila Costa perde vaga ao Senado e concorrerá à Câmara: 'Impacto da ausência de Michelle'
item.description: Priscila Costa (PL-CE), an ally of former First Lady Michelle Bolsonaro, lost her Senate candidacy after Michelle resigned from PL Mulher and withdrew from party articulations. She will now run for federal deputy, after being blocked by the party from running for Senate due to a Ceará-based composition favoring Alcides Fernandes, father of André Fernandes. Priscila was also removed as Secretary-General of PL Ceará, now holding only a titular role as a votary in the state directory.

item.title: Tarifaço: governo não desiste da negociação, mas só vê o caminho aberto com os EUA após as eleições
item.description: The Lula government continues negotiating with the U.S. to reverse the tariff hike but believes a solution will only be possible after the October 2026 elections, as Washington prefers to wait for the electoral outcome to avoid giving an advantage to the PT. Although the Economic Reciprocity Law remains an option, the government chooses caution to avoid bolstering Bolsonarist rhetoric, preserving diplomatic channels and seeking to mitigate export impacts while awaiting the post-electoral scenario.

item.title: Lula diz que Brasil não vai ficar 'chorando' por exportações que não irão aos EUA e que diálogo não teve reciprocidade
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva stated that Brazil will not 'cry' over exports lost to the U.S. due to new 25% tariffs, and affirmed it will remain at the negotiation table with its proposals despite lack of reciprocity. He emphasized Brazil will seek alternative markets and that there is no veto to negotiation, even as the U.S. imposed tariffs on goods linked to PIX and digital platforms.

item.title: Ao vivo: Lula sanciona destinação de recursos para o Brasil Soberano
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva signed PLV No. 7 of 2026, allocating resources to the Brazil Sovereign program, designed to support companies affected by U.S. import tariffs. The initiative aims to preserve jobs, strengthen productive capacity, and enhance the competitiveness of Brazilian firms. The signing ceremony took place at 3 p.m.

item.title: Lula anuncia R$ 18,5 bilhões para empresas afetadas pelo tarifaço
item.description: President Lula announced a provisional measure allocating R$ 18.5 billion to support Brazilian companies affected by 25% U.S. tariffs on products such as biofuels, chemicals, machinery, footwear, and apparel. The funding is part of the third phase of the Brazil Sovereign Plan and aims to offset estimated export losses of up to US$ 11 billion. The announcement coincided with the tariffs taking effect.

item.title: Lula libera R$ 18,5 bilhões em crédito para empresas afetadas por tarifaço do governo Trump
item.description: President Lula announced the release of R$18.5 billion in credit for companies affected by U.S. tariffs and the Middle East war, complementing a law that already allocated R$15 billion to the Brazil Sovereign Plan. The measures aim to support sectors such as industry, agriculture, and mining, with conditions like job maintenance, following negotiations with the U.S. that proved unfruitful due to U.S. demands deemed non-negotiable, including changes to PIX and critical minerals legislation.

item.title: Planalto anuncia socorro de R$ 18,5 bi para setores atingidos pelo tarifaço dos EUA
item.description: The federal government announced an R$18.5 billion credit package for exporters and supply chains affected by U.S. tariffs and the Middle East war, covering industry, agribusiness, mining, fishing, aquaculture, and forestry. President Lula also sanctioned a law allocating R$15 billion to the Brazil Sovereign Plan, expanding credit access during international trade instability. Beneficiary companies must preserve part of their workforce as a condition.

item.title: Flávio usará colete à prova de balas em eventos públicos
item.description: Senator and presidential pre-candidate Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) will begin wearing bulletproof vests at public events due to an increase in threats identified by his security team. The measure, reported by Folha de S.Paulo, aims to ensure his physical safety during public appearances. His protection is carried out by Federal Police agents.

item.title: Governo Lula anuncia R$ 18,5 bilhões em crédito para socorrer setores afetados por tarifaço de Trump
item.description: The Lula government announced R$18.5 billion in subsidized credit through the Brazil Sovereign plan to support companies affected by the new U.S. tariffs. The measure aims to mitigate the impact of American trade measures and international uncertainty, taking effect on the same day the U.S. tariffs come into force.
